newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China beefs up PLA troops in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China beefs up PLA troops in Hong Kong.

text.p: The People's Liberation Army (PLA) almost doubled its advance guard in Hong Kong with a fresh contingent of soldiers on Friday to gear up for the British colony's historic merger with China in 32 days time.

A convoy of 90 PLA troops in 12 military vehicles drove over the border to join 106 soldiers already stationed in Hong Kong taking over barracks for a garrison eventually expected to be up to 10,000 strong.
London is handing its last Asian colony back to China at midnight on June 30, when the PLA will take over defence duties from the withdrawing British armed forces.
The latest team of 17 PLA field officers, 44 junior officers and 29 soldiers was greeted at the border by advance unit commander General Zhou Borong and Hong Kong security officials.
They are expected to be deployed in six military sites including the Osborn Barracks which Britain vacates on Saturday.
In April London and Beijing agreed China could send advance troops into Hong Kong so long as they were unarmed and did not wear their uniforms in public when off duty.

The formation of the PLA garrison was completed in China last year and the units have been stationed until now in Shenzhen, just across the border from Hong Kong, occasionally staging charm offensives by inviting Hong Kong media to see their drilling and military exercises.
The garrison will be made up of ground, naval and air forces, and will be subject to strict political, military and disciplinary training, Chinese officials have said.
Its duties will be to defend Hong Kong from external attack and demonstrate China's sovereignty over the area, which will be known as the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Britain has been steadily winding down its military presence in this bustling capitalist metropolis of 6.4 million people.

Only 1,000 British military and civilian personnel remain in the British garrison, down from 10,000 in its heyday several years ago. The remaining defence forces include about 400 soldiers, drawn mainly from the Black Watch regiment.
China has promised it will be sending elite troops of the highest calibre and moral fibre and that they will be on tiptop behaviour.
However, many in Hong Kong have jittery memories of the PLA's actions in 1989 when its tanks rolled into Beijing's Tiananmen Square to crush a student protest movement with a heavy loss of life.
